audit_status: PASS: arithmetic and billing-scope correction independently verified; performance ratio not independently reproduced.

sources.claim_audited: Post labels CPU-only amounts as full bare-metal costs and claims roughly 10-12x token economics. It reports up-to-5x/6x throughput for two scenarios, without absolute throughput or reproducible run artifacts.

sources.fact: Separately lists .0119/OCPU-hour and .0114/GB-hour beside the 120-OCPU/1152GB bare-metal shape.
X9 CPU and memory are separately charged; bare-metal allocations are fixed. Boot and block volumes are additional.

sources.verification: Independently visually inspected pricing-056.png. Four selected SKU rates match API; notes say both bare metal and virtual machine.

important_limits: 5x and6x are separate up-to performance claims, not a confidence interval or typical range. Present scenario-conditioned results only.
Correction is CPU plus memory list billing, not total cost of ownership: excludes storage, network charges, software, support, taxes and discounts.
Accepting reported throughput still gives X12 an advantage in those scenarios; the correction does not show Intel is uneconomic.
This is an Intel generation comparison, not Intel versus AMD or Arm; do not connect these ratios to the existing2.9% cross-vendor breakeven.
Current API and dated launch/article support the price components; historical invoice amounts and private discounts are unknown.
Blog gives no numerical TTFT/ITL results, quality equivalence, exact model quantization, binary commit or run distributions sufficient to independently replicate its throughput.
120 minus64 equals56, so the blog’s88-core-increase statement is inconsistent; do not repeat it.
No direction or size of Intel margin, ASP or valuation change is identified by this billing correction.
author_followup_questions: In the July20 X12/X9 comparison, was memory included in the stated full-node prices? The published CPU and memory rates imply14.5608/h and4.096/h before other charges; is a different discount or billing scope intended?
Can you share public raw token throughput and TTFT/ITL results, quantization, llama.cpp commit/flags, run counts and identical quality settings for each scenario?
Is there a comparable E6Ax run or a workload where X12 does not win, and how should the deployment decision change in that case?
recommended_exhibit_claim: At published CPU-plus-memory rates, accepting the two reported throughput scenarios implies about1.41x or1.69x work per dollar, rather than the post’s roughly10-12x claim. Performance was not rerun.
